In $Q_8=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$, take $X=\{i,-i,j,-j\}$.
Then $H=Q_8$, $|Z|=2$, $k=2$, and
\[
|\Good(\Conj X)|=4=\min(8,2^2),\qquad |\Aut(\Conj X)|=8.
\]

In the above setting, assume $|Z|\geq2$. Then
\[
|\Good(\Conj X)|=|Z|^k
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
zO^{-1}=O\quad\text{for every }z\in Z,\ O\in\Omega.
\]
Whenever these equivalent conditions hold, equality also holds in
\eqref{eq:bound}.

no_target_yet.statement:
A conjugation subquandle $X$ is inverse-closed if and only if
inversion permutes its conjugation orbits; it need not fix each orbit.
Thus the orbitwise assertion in Ta's Remark 2.14 (v5, p.~6),
``every element $x\in X$ is conjugate to its inverse $x^{-1}$'',
does not follow from inverse-closure alone.

If the center term is attained, then $X\cap Z=\varnothing$,
$Z\subseteq[H,H]$, the abelianization of $H$ has exponent at most two,
and $|Z|$ divides every orbit size. In particular $|Z|^2$ divides $|H|$.
If $X$ meets the center, the center-term inequality is strict.

Then $X$ generates $H$, $|Z(H)|=2^d$, $|X/H|=3^d$, and

no_target_yet.statement:
For both values of $t$, $X$ generates $H_{m,t}$, the center has order
two, and $X$ has two conjugation orbits. Moreover
\[
|\Aut(\Conj X)|=m\varphi(m),\qquad
|\Good(\Conj X)|=
\begin{cases}4,&4\mid m,\\2,&m\equiv2\pmod4,\end{cases}
\]
where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient. Thus \eqref{eq:bound} is attained
exactly when $4\mid m$.
The good-involution counts reprove Kamada--Oshiro~\cite[Theorem~3.2]{ko}
and Ta~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{ta} for these realizations.

For the reflection quandle $R_m$ above,
\[
\operatorname{Anti}R_m=\Aut R_m
=\{a\mapsto u+va:\ u\in\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z,\
v\in(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^\times\}.
\]
Thus $\Aut R_m\cup\operatorname{Anti}R_m$ is the affine group
$(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)\rtimes(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^\times$.
There are three symmetric-isomorphism classes $(R_m,\rho)$ when
$4\mid m$, and two when $m\equiv2\pmod4$.
